title: High-Resolution Multiparameter DNA Flow Cytometry for Accurate Ploidy Assessment and the Detection and Sorting of Tumor and Stromal Subpopulations from Paraffin-Embedded Tissues
protocol: Label epithelial cells with FITC-conjugated antibody against keratin.
Label stromal cells with RPE, APC, or Alexa Fluor 647 (AF647)-conjugated antibody against vimentin.
Stain DNA content with DAPI or PI.
Measure fluorescence using a flow cytometer equipped with UV (355 nm), violet (405 nm), blue (488 nm), and red (633 nm) excitation lasers.
Obtain a nylon biopsy bag.
Resize larger bags as necessary.
Ensure the width of the bag is wider than the diameter of the glass tube.
Cut away superfluous nylon using a pair of scissors.
Tightly close an open boundary of the nylon bag with tweezers, keeping the legs parallel to the opening.
Melt the nylon with a small flame from a cigarette lighter to seal the boundary.
Seal three of the four boundaries of the nylon bag, leaving one open.
Select the area of interest on the H&E-stained FFPE tissue section using a waterproof marker under a light microscope.
Prepare a clean recipient paraffin block.
Drill 2.0-mm-diameter cores in the recipient block using the red recipient puncher by simultaneously punching and swinging the puncher sideways.
Orient the marked-up H&E-stained section to match the contours of the corresponding tissue in the paraffin tissue block.
Copy the boundaries of the marked-up area on the tissue block using a permanent marker.
Punch 2.0-mm-diameter tissue cores within the marked-up area using a tissue arrayer (blue donor punch).
Transfer the punched tissues to the pre-drilled empty cores in the recipient block.
Store the block overnight at 37°C.
Cut FFPE tissue sections and collect tissue.
Deparaffinize the collected tissue sections.
Collect the 60-μm sections in the nylon bag via the last opening.
Close the nylon bag as described.
Put the bag containing the tissue roll(s) at the bottom of a clean 10.0-ml Pyrex glass disposable culture tube(s).
Add 5.0 ml of 100% xylene to the glass tube(s) until the nylon bag with the tissue roll(s) is completely immersed.
If using C-Tubes, add 5.0 ml of 100% xylene to the C-Tube(s) with the section(s).
Let stand for 10 min at room temperature in the safety cabinet.
Discard the xylene.
Re-immersse the sections in the tube(s) or bag completely in fresh xylene.
Let stand for another 10 min at room temperature.
Repeat step 3, substep h.
Discard the 100% xylene.
Rehydrate the sample by sequential incubation in each of the following: 100% ethanol, three 5-min changes.
Rehydrate the sample by sequential incubation in each of the following: 70% ethanol, three 5-min changes.
Rehydrate the sample by sequential incubation in each of the following: 50% ethanol, three 5-min changes.
Rehydrate the sample by sequential incubation in each of the following: Milli-Q water, once for 5 min.
Substitute the Milli-Q water with HIAR buffer, pH 6.4, at room temperature.
Immerse the bag completely in HIAR buffer.
Refresh the HIAR buffer after 5 min with prewarmed HIAR buffer (80°C).
Place the sample tube in an 80°C water bath for 60 min.
Take out the tube containing the sample bag from the 80°C water bath and let it cool down to room temperature.
Wash the sample twice, each time for 5 min with PBS.
Replace the PBS with plain RPMI 1640 medium, pH 7.6.
Replace RPMI 1640 medium with prewarmed dissociation solution.
Ensure the nylon bag containing the sample is completely immersed in the RPMI-enzyme mixture.
Incubate the sample 30 to 120 min in a 37°C water bath.
Swirl the sample on a vortex every 15 min until tissue sections disintegrate for nylon bags.
Put C-Tube(s) in the gentleMACSTM after 15 min of incubation and select program 3.2: SPLEEN followed by RUN (16 sec).
Repeat the dissociation process every 15 min until tissue sections are disintegrated.
Take a small aliquot from the sample (10 μl), put it in a 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tube, and add 40 μl of hematoxylin.
Mix well and count the number of cells using a Bürker counter chamber and a standard microscope.
Stop the dissociation process by putting the sample on ice as soon as the cell numbers of two consecutive 15-min counts are approximately identical.
Transfer cells through a 100-μm mesh nylon filter into a FACS tube.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 minutes at 1000 × g using a pre-cooled centrifuge at 4°C.
Wash the cell pellet twice with 2 ml of ice-cold PBATw.
Discard the supernatant after each wash.
Add 2 ml of ice-cold PBATw to the cell pellet, vortex the mixture.
Take a 10-μl sample and put it in a 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tube.
Dilute cells 1:5 in hematoxylin and count cells using a Bürker counter chamber and standard microscope.
Perform immunocytochemistry for keratin and vimentin, and DNA labeling for UV or violet and blue excitation.
Take four 12 × 75–mm tubes and pipette 1 × 106 cells in each tube.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 minutes at 1000 × g using a pre-cooled centrifuge at 4°C.
Stain different cell fractions, including controls, for keratin, vimentin, and DNA according to the specified scheme.
Add 100 μl of primary reagent to the tube, vortex gently until the pellet is completely dissolved.
Incubate overnight at 4°C in PBATw.
Wash twice with 1 ml ice-cold PBATw by centrifuging for 5 min at 1000 × g, 4°C and removing supernatant after each wash.
Add 100 μl of secondary reagents (mixture of GaMIgG1-FITC and GaMIgG2b-RPE) to the pellets, vortex gently until completely dissolved.
Place tubes on ice.
Wash twice with 1 ml PBATw.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 1000 × g at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant after each wash.
Add 0.5 ml DNA staining solution containing DAPI to the cell pellets.
Vortex gently until the pellet is completely dissolved (approximately 5 seconds).
Store in the dark for at least 2 hours before analysis.
Filter all samples over a nylon mesh of 50-μm to prevent clogging of the flow cytometer.
Perform multiparameter DNA measurement of cell suspensions from FFPE carcinomas.
Design a layout displaying bivariate dot plots and single-parameter histograms for data acquisition and sorting.
Acquire data from the sample tube stained with DAPI alone.
Place a threshold on the FSC (i.e., 5000 at 256 × 100 channel resolution) in combination with a threshold on the DAPI detector.

Adjust the PMT settings of the DAPI fluorescence detector until the first G0G1 peak is approximately positioned at one fifth of the linear scale (i.e., channel 50,000 at 256 × 100 channel resolution).
Create an electronic region/gate R1 around the G0G1 peak and color-code this gate in the FSC–SSC dot plot.
Adjust the FSC settings until all colored events show up to the right of the FSC threshold.

Draw a second electronic region/gate R2 around the single-cell events of the 355 DNA-DAPI 450/50-A or Height versus 355 DNA-DAPI 450/50-A bivariate dot plot and activate this region/gate R2 in the other dot plots and histograms.
Adjust PMT settings to show a log-normal distribution in the first log-decade of the 4-decade FITC or RPE detector.
Take the vimentin-positive sample and adjust for RPE spillover into the FITC and DAPI fluorescence detectors.
Repeat adjustment for keratin-positive sample, adjusting for FITC spillover into the RPE and DAPI fluorescence detectors.
Acquire and store events for multiparameter DNA analysis of samples labeled with DAPI, FITC, and RPE.
Stop acquisition when >20,000 single keratin-positive events are collected within R2 using a 1024-channel resolution scale.
Store the data in the computer, including all collected events.
Design a layout displaying specified bivariate dot plots and single-parameter histograms for immunophenotypic analysis of flow cytometry data.
Create bivariate dot plots: FSC (lin) versus SSC (lin).
Create bivariate dot plot: 355 DNA-DAPI 450/50-A (lin) or Height (lin) versus 355 DNA-DAPI 450/50-A (lin).
Create bivariate dot plot: 355 DNA-DAPI 450/50-A (lin) versus green FITC fluorescence (biexponential).
Create bivariate dot plot: 355 DNA-DAPI 450/50 A (lin) versus orange (RPE) fluorescence (biexponential).
Create bivariate dot plot: Green (FITC) fluorescence (biexponential) vs. Orange (RPE) fluorescence (biexponential).
Create single-parameter histograms for green FITC fluorescence.
Create single-parameter histograms for orange RPE fluorescence.
Create three 355 DNA-DAPI 450/50 A (lin) histograms: one ungated and two gated histograms for cell cycle distribution analysis.
Open the data file of DAPI-labeled cells only.
Create an analysis region R1 around single events, excluding debris and aggregates using the specified bivariate dot plot.
Activate R1 in the following bivariate dot plots and single parameter histograms.
Plot DNA-DAPI 450/50 A (linear scale) versus green (FITC) fluorescence (biexponential).
Plot DNA-DAPI 450/50 A (linear scale) versus orange (RPE) fluorescence (biexponential).
Plot green (FITC) fluorescence (biexponential) versus orange (RPE) fluorescence (biexponential).
Create a histogram for green (FITC) fluorescence (biexponential).
Create a histogram for orange (RPE) fluorescence (biexponential).
Open the data file of the vimentin-positive control.
Compensate fluorescence signals when applicable based on flow cytometer type and data file format.
Adjust spectral spillover of RPE fluorescence in DAPI fluorescence until vimentin-positive events are parallel to the ordinate axis.
Create a region R2 around the vimentin-positive events.
Activate gate R2 in the first DNA-DAPI 450/50 A (linear scale) histogram.
Open the data file of the keratin-positive control.
Correct for spectral spillover of FITC into RPE and DAPI parameters when necessary.
Ensure keratin-positive events are parallel to the ordinate axis of the DNA-DAPI 450/50 A (linear scale) versus green (FITC) fluorescence bivariate dot plot.
Create a region R3 around the keratin-positive events.
Activate this gate in the second 355 DNA-DAPI 450/50 A (lin) histogram.
Load the data file containing the triply stained cells.
Make small final spectral spillover adjustments when required.
Create a region R4 around the G0G1 population of the DNA histogram composed of the vimentin-positive events.
Calculate the median fluorescence using the software.
Create a region R5 around the G0G1 population of the DNA histogram composed of the keratin-positive events.
Calculate the median fluorescence using the software.
Do the same for other G0G1 populations when present in the keratin-positive population.
Prepare cell suspensions from FFPE tissues.
Add 100 μl of secondary reagents (mixture of GaMIgG1-FITC or GaMIgG1-Alexa FluorTM 488 and GaMIgG2b-APC) to the pellets and gently vortex until the pellet is completely dissolved.
Place tubes on ice.
Wash twice with 1 ml PBATw, centrifuging for 5 min at 1000 × g, 4°C, removing the supernatant after each wash.
Add 0.5 ml DNA staining solution with PI to each of the cell pellets and vortex gently.
Put the tubes in a 37°C water bath for 30 min.
Store in the dark at 2°C to 8°C (refrigerator) for at least 2 hr before analysis.
Perform overnight DNA labeling at 2°C to 8°C in the refrigerator.
Filter all samples over a 50-μm nylon mesh before acquisition.
Measure multiparameter DNA of cell suspensions from FFPE carcinomas and flow cytometry data analysis.
Replace orange (488 RPE 575/26-A) fluorescence parameters with red (633 APC or Alexa FluorTM 647 670/14-A) fluorescence parameters for stromal cell fraction analysis.
Replace the DAPI-DNA 450/50-A (lin) parameter with DNA-PI 610/20-A (lin) or DNA-PI 670-A (lin) parameter for DNA content analysis.
Prepare cell suspension from FFPE tissues as described in the Basic Protocol.
Follow steps 4 to 11 of the Basic Protocol for cell staining.
Add 0.5 ml PI staining solution containing RNase to the cell pellets and vortex gently.
Incubate tubes in a 37°C water bath for 30 min.
Store samples in the dark at refrigerator temperature for at least 2 hr before analysis.
Obtain best results after an overnight DNA labeling at 2°C to 8°C in the refrigerator.
Filter all samples over a 50-μm nylon mesh before acquisition to prevent clogging of the flow cytometer.
Perform multiparameter DNA measurement of cell suspensions from FFPE carcinomas and flow cytometry data analysis.
Follow step 12 to 24 of the Basic Protocol.
Replace the 355 DAPI-DNA 450/50-A (lin) parameter by the 488 DNA-PI >650-A (lin).
Use the 488 DNA-PI >670-A (lin) depending on flow cytometer parameters.
Sort vimentin-positive stromal cell fraction using a four-way cell sorter.
Simultaneously sort up to three tumor subpopulations during the sorting process.
Use a DEPArray for imaging and digital-sorting of small tumor samples.
Detect DNA variants in low-tumor-cell percentage samples reliably.
Equip a flow cytometer with sorting capabilities.
Follow steps 1 to 11 of the Basic Protocol for sample preparation and cell staining.
Display dot plots and histograms as described in the Basic Protocol.
Design a gating strategy to sort stromal, vimentin-positive cell fraction and keratin-positive cell fraction.
Sort cells into 12 × 75–mm tubes or directly into 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge sorted cells at 3000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Extract DNA using proteinase K at 56°C overnight or use a commercial kit according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Inactivate proteinase K for 10 minutes at 100°C.
